source.note: Scan without a text layer (Adobe PDF Library 9.0). National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF has 16 pages: the question paper (printed pages 1–13, PDF page n = printed page n), TWO diagram sheets (PDF page 14 = DIAGRAM SHEET 1 for QUESTIONS 2.1 and 2.2; PDF page 15 = DIAGRAM SHEET 2 for QUESTION 12) and the information sheet (PDF page 16). The cover states that the question paper consists of 13 pages, 2 diagram sheets and 1 information sheet. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: The five-number summary of the heights of trees three months after they were planted is $(23\,;\,42\,;\,50\,;\,53\,;\,75)$. This information is shown in the box and whisker diagram below.

questions.text_md: Determine the interquartile range.
What percentage of plants has a height in excess of $53$ cm?
Between which quartiles do the heights of the trees have the least variation? Explain.

questions.stem_md: The relationship between blood alcohol levels and the risk of having a car accident has been studied for years. Research has shown the following results:

table.caption: Blood alcohol level (%) and relative risk of having a car accident (%)
header: RELATIVE RISK OF HAVING A CAR ACCIDENT (%)

questions.text_md: Draw a scatter plot on DIAGRAM SHEET $1$ to represent the data.
Draw a line (or curve) of best fit on DIAGRAM SHEET $1$.
questions.notes: The paper allows a line or a curve of best fit, as printed.

questions.text_md: Describe the trend of the data.
Estimate the probability of having a car accident when one's blood alcohol level is $0{,}18\%$. (The legal limit of the blood alcohol level is $0{,}05\%$.)
questions.notes: The table and axes are labelled relative risk, but the question asks for a probability, as printed.

questions.stem_md: The cumulative frequency curve (ogive) drawn below shows the time taken (in minutes) for $140$ patrons to leave an auditorium after watching a show.

questions.text_md: Estimate the number of people who took more than $15$ minutes to leave the auditorium.
Estimate the number of people who took between $8$ and $12$ minutes to leave the auditorium.
Write down the modal class for the data.

questions.stem_md:
The Grade $10$ classes of three schools wrote a term test. All three schools have the same number of learners in Grade $10$. The results of the tests have been summarised in the table below.

The distribution of the results is shown in the diagram below.

table.caption: Mean and standard deviation of term-test marks at three schools

questions.text_md: In which school (A, B or C) is the majority of the results more widely spread around the mean? Give a reason for your answer.
What is the difference in the spread around the respective means of the marks in School A and School C?
Explain how the marks of School A must be adjusted to match the marks of School C.
If each mark in School C is lowered by $10\%$, explain the effect it will have on the mean and standard deviation of this school.
questions.notes: A multiplicative change of $10\%$ to every mark; no dedicated skill for the effect of scaling on mean and standard deviation.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, $\mathrm{P}$ is a point $(-5\,;\,0)$. The inclination of line $\mathrm{PT}$ is $63{,}43^{\circ}$. $\mathrm{S}$ is the midpoint and the $y$-intercept of $\mathrm{PT}$. $\mathrm{R}$ is a point on the $x$-axis such that $\mathrm{PO}:\mathrm{OR}=2:3$.

questions.text_md: The gradient of $\mathrm{PT}$, correct to the nearest integer value
The equation of $\mathrm{PT}$ in the form $y=mx+c$
The distance $\mathrm{PS}$ in surd form
The coordinates of $\mathrm{T}$
Determine the coordinates of $\mathrm{R}$.
questions.notes: Uses the given ratio $\mathrm{PO}:\mathrm{OR}=2:3$ on the $x$-axis. No dedicated section-formula skill; ageo.distance-formula is the closest.

questions.text_md: Calculate the area of $\triangle\mathrm{PTR}$.
questions.notes: Area of a triangle in the coordinate plane; no dedicated coordinate-area skill.

questions.stem_md:
In the diagram below, $\mathrm{M}$ is the centre of the circle having the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}-6x+2y-8=0$. The circle passes through $\mathrm{R}(0\,;\,-4)$ and $\mathrm{N}(p\,;\,q)$.

$\mathrm{R}\hat{\mathrm{M}}\mathrm{N}=90^{\circ}$. The tangents drawn to the circle at $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{N}$ meet at $\mathrm{P}$.

questions.text_md: Show that $\mathrm{M}$ is the point $(3\,;\,-1)$.
Determine the equation of $\mathrm{MR}$ in the form $y=mx+c$.
Show that $q=2-p$.
Determine the values of $p$ and $q$.
Determine the equation of the circle having centre $\mathrm{O}$ and passing through $\mathrm{N}$.
Calculate the area of the circle centred at $\mathrm{M}$.
Calculate the ratio in its simplest form: $\dfrac{\mathrm{NP}}{\mathrm{MP}}$
Determine the image of $\mathrm{P}(x\,;\,y)$ if $\mathrm{P}$ is rotated through $90^{\circ}$ about the origin in a clockwise direction and then reflected about the $y$-axis.
Determine the image of $\mathrm{P}(x\,;\,y)$ if $\mathrm{P}$ is reflected about the $y$-axis and then rotated through $90^{\circ}$ about the origin in a clockwise direction.

questions.stem_md:
Mo and Ziya argue about the image of $\mathrm{P}(x\,;\,y)$ under the following transformations:

* Rotation through $90^{\circ}$ about the origin in a clockwise direction
* Reflection about the $y$-axis

Mo claims that the order in which the transformations are performed will affect the final position of the image. Ziya argues that the final position of the image will be the same, irrespective of the order in which the transformations are performed.
questions.text_md: Which of the two, Mo or Ziya, is correct in this case? Explain.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{ABC}$ is an isosceles triangle such that vertex $\mathrm{C}$ lies at $(0\,;\,-1)$. $\mathrm{AB}$ is parallel to the $x$-axis and $\mathrm{AC}=\sqrt{10}$.

questions.text_md: A rigid transformation is applied to $\triangle\mathrm{ABC}$ to obtain $\triangle\mathrm{PQR}$ as shown. $\mathrm{R}(-4\,;\,3)$ is the image of $\mathrm{C}$. Describe fully, in words, the transformation from $\triangle\mathrm{ABC}$ to $\triangle\mathrm{PQR}$.
$\triangle\mathrm{PQR}$ is reflected about the line $y=x$. Determine the coordinates of $\mathrm{R}'$, the image of $\mathrm{R}$.

questions.stem_md:
$\triangle\mathrm{ABC}$ is enlarged through the origin to obtain $\triangle\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{C}'$ such that:

$\dfrac{\text{area of }\triangle\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{C}'}{\text{area of }\triangle\mathrm{ABC}}=16$

questions.text_md: Determine the scale factor of the enlargement.
If $\mathrm{AC}=\sqrt{10}$ units, write down the length of $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{C}'$.

After a rigid transformation is applied to $\triangle\mathrm{ABC}$ to obtain $\triangle\mathrm{DEF}$, $\mathrm{F}(0\,;\,1)$ is the image of $\mathrm{C}$. If $\mathrm{E}$ is the point $(s\,;\,t)$, write down an equation in terms of $s$ and $t$.

questions.stem_md:
A wheel is positioned so that its centre is directly on the origin in the Cartesian plane.

$\mathrm{T}\left(-\dfrac{16}{\sqrt{2}}\,;\,\dfrac{16}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ is a point on the outer edge of the wheel.

When the wheel is rotated in a clockwise direction about the origin through an angle of $\theta$, $\mathrm{T}$ is directly on $\mathrm{W}(8\,;\,-8\sqrt{3})$.

questions.text_md: Show that $\theta=195^{\circ}$.

When the wheel is rotated at a uniform speed in a clockwise direction, it takes $1{,}3$ seconds for $\mathrm{T}$ to travel to $\mathrm{W}$. Calculate the speed, in revolutions per minute, at which the wheel is rotated.
questions.notes: Uniform rotational speed from a $195^{\circ}$ turn in $1{,}3$ seconds, expressed in revolutions per minute. No dedicated angular-speed skill.

questions.stem_md:
In the diagram below, reflex $\mathrm{T}\hat{\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{P}=\alpha$ and $\mathrm{P}$ has coordinates $(-5\,;\,-12)$.

Determine the value of each of the following trigonometric ratios WITHOUT using a calculator:

questions.text_md: $\cos\alpha$
$\tan(180^{\circ}-\alpha)$
$\sin(30^{\circ}-\alpha)$
Prove the following identity:  $\dfrac{\cos^{2}(90^{\circ}+\theta)}{\cos(-\theta)+\sin(90^{\circ}-\theta)\cos\theta}=\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}-1$
Determine the general solution of: $\tan x\sin x+\cos x\tan x=0$.
questions.notes: Equation confirmed at 400 dpi as $\tan x\sin x+\cos x\tan x=0$.

questions.text_md: Simplify the expression to a single trigonometric ratio of $x$.
Write down the maximum value of the expression.

questions.stem_md: Determine the following trigonometric ratios in terms of $p$ and/or $q$:

questions.text_md: (a)  $\cos 2\alpha$
(b)  $\tan\alpha$
Simplify $\dfrac{p}{2q}-\dfrac{q}{2p}$ to a single trigonometric ratio of $\alpha$.
questions.notes: The printed expression was confirmed at 400 dpi as $\dfrac{p}{2q}-\dfrac{q}{2p}$.

questions.text_md: Draw the graphs of $f(x)=\tan x+1$ and $g(x)=\cos 2x$ for $x\in[-180^{\circ}\,;\,180^{\circ}]$ on the same system of axes provided on DIAGRAM SHEET $2$. Clearly show all intercepts with the axes, turning points and asymptotes.
Write down the period of $g$.
If $h(x)=-\cos 2(x+10^{\circ})$, describe fully, in words, the transformation from $g$ to $h$.
For which values of $x$, where $x>0$, will $f'(x)g(x)>0$?

questions.stem_md: The Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt was built around $2\,500$ BC. The pyramid has a square base $(\mathrm{ABCD})$ with sides $232{,}6$ metres long. The distance from each corner of the base to the apex $(\mathrm{E})$ was originally $221{,}2$ metres.

questions.text_md: Calculate the size of the angle at the apex of a face of the pyramid (for example $\mathrm{C}\hat{\mathrm{E}}\mathrm{B}$).
Calculate the angle each face makes with the base (for example $\mathrm{E}\hat{\mathrm{F}}\mathrm{G}$, where $\mathrm{EF}\perp\mathrm{AB}$ in $\triangle\mathrm{AEB}$).
